notes: Verified: go build ./..., go vet (incl. -tags integration for httpapi), go test -race ./internal/mcpoauth (uncached) and ./internal/httpapi all pass.

Unit tests genuinely exercise the target: signature/issuer/exp/nbf/typ=ID/cnf/sub/audience/scope/account refusals each assert status+cause via a real fake IdP with JWKS; the disabled-installation case asserts the pre-existing invalid_token message and zero account lookups; wildcard-in-ceiling and admin '*' role are asserted to never survive ApplyOAuthCeiling.
internal/httpapi/mcp_oauth_integration_test.go is behind //go:build integration and QURIO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN; it compiles but was not executed here (no Postgres in this session).

Feature is off by default (mcp.oauth.enabled=false); with it off the /mcp 401 path, body and headers are byte-identical to before (asserted in tests). Fully revertible: only new settings rows, no migration.

Design gaps that are documented rather than defects: OAuth principals skip the per-key rate limiter (internal/httpapi/middleware.go:334 only rate-limits api_key); every AuthType != "api_key" resource-scope helper (APIKeyScopeAllowed, resourceScopeSQLFilter, legacy defaultScopeAllowed, platformapi job_scopes) treats oauth as scope-unrestricted, which equals a key with no resource scopes as the commit states.

internal/mcpoauth/mcpoauth.go:providerFor holds s.mu across oidc.NewProvider (up to 15s http timeout), so all /mcp SSO auths serialize while Keycloak discovery is down; negative cache is 5s so the impact is bounded.
Trusting azp alone (mcp.oauth.audience) means any token minted for that public client is accepted regardless of aud; this is the documented no-mapper path and admin-controlled.
internal/webui/dist rebuilt (16 hashed chunks) — routine for feature commits in this repo (see 7af0883).
